<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **218** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **157** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **157**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `12b2d7416b067f7a5b2ff6269acffce02eb8b91b` — the merge of head `abde58e1ebeeb1d9b90285689286c2f3ed755b0f` into base `0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 12b2d7416b067f7a5b2ff6269acffce02eb8b91b && git checkout 12b2d7416b067f7a5b2ff6269acffce02eb8b91b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd abde58e1ebeeb1d9b90285689286c2f3ed755b0f && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd && git merge --no-ff abde58e1ebeeb1d9b90285689286c2f3ed755b0f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `72a8bffd9fa53f37ade9a33e0e3e80ab0e825a27`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.user-field-delete-behavior-enforced.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.user-field-foreign-reference-refused.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine.ts on the head (`statesDeleteSemantics`, `deleteWalkTargetOf`, `cascadeRelationBehavior`, `walkReferencingRelations`, `getCascadeDeleteObjects`), packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts (`SemanticMigration`), packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.field-master-detail-set-null-refused.ts (the precedent), packages/spec/src/data/form-delete-behavior-options.test.ts (the pin and its evaluator), .changeset/29253-user-field-delete-behavior.md, .changeset/29415-user-delete-behavior-entry.md, .changeset/28001-cascade-delete-objects-beside-item.md, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs (the foreign-changeset rule), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx (the select widget the forms' `deleteBehavior` row renders through)

Inputs read: card #29415, body and all 8 comments; PR #29553's 5 comments (triage record 6588315424, PASS on `59709cbb`; hold 6588339023; supersession 6593912044); PR #29712's body, its 15-file list and the net diff against `main` at the merge base `1c1a5d40` (+150 / −42); the 69 check-runs on `72a8bffd` (56 success, 10 skipped, 3 failure) and the logs of the three reds. The cited code was read with `git show` on the head; nothing was checked out, built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set: nothing moves — right.** `FieldSchema.deleteBehavior` stays `z.enum(['set_null','cascade','restrict']).optional()` with the same `.overwrite` (materializes `set_null` on `lookup` / `tree` only). The `user`-field `reference` refusal changes its message text only, same issue path. No export, type or authorable key is added, removed or re-shaped; `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface` and `check:docs` are green inside `TypeScript Type Check`.
2. **The semantic entry `user-field-delete-behavior-enforced` — right shape, right content.** A `SemanticMigration` and not a conversion: no key or value moved, and whether a declaration was meant is the author's to say — the `field-master-detail-set-null-refused` and `user-field-foreign-reference-refused` precedents. It is collected by `gen:migration-registry` into the gitignored registry, so it is no public export; `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` are green. `conversionIds` is rightly omitted (no conversion judges it) and `relevantWhen` is rightly omitted (0 of the 536 semantic entries declare one, and the surface lives under object fields, not a top-level stack key).
3. **The DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/29253-user-field-delete-behavior.md` — right, each sentence judged.** The diff moves exactly two lines of that pending note:
   - the adr-0087 marker comment, from `not-required (no-migration-prescription) … there is no stored value for a conversion to rewrite …` to `registered user-field-delete-behavior-enforced`. True on this head: the id resolves to the entry this diff adds, `check-adr-0087-registration` (its R3 / R4 batteries read exactly this) is green in `Lint & Repo Gates`, and the old text contradicted the note's own "Rows stored before #9784" paragraph.
   - appended to that paragraph: "No conversion rewrites it, because whether the value was meant is the author's to say: the semantic migration entry `user-field-delete-behavior-enforced` lists it for `objectstack migrate meta` and the upgrade guide. Save the object again without the key, or with the value you want." True against the entry's `acceptanceCriteria` and against the engine: no conversion is registered, and the remedy is the entry's own.
   Nothing else in the note moves, and neither sentence restores a false statement. Both `Check Changeset` reds (runs 41566264692 and 41566690439; the second is the rerun after #29553 closed) are the #17712 foreign-changeset refusal on this one file and nothing else — the log names the file and prints the two-class remedy. The landing rule for a diff that also changes code is 「其余(含改代码)照全套:同 head 达档复核 PASS 记录即确认,记录逐句判改写句」; this record is that confirmation.
4. **The forms — right.** The `lookup` `deleteBehavior` row's `visibleWhen` becomes `data.type in ['lookup','user']` in both `field.form.ts` and `object.form.ts`; the `master_detail` row stays disjoint; `tree` stays unserved (pre-existing, inherited note). A Studio surface change, not a metadata-protocol change: the key was already accepted on `user`.
5. **Gate verdicts on the head.** 56 success, 10 skipped, 3 failure. The two `Check Changeset` reds are item 3. The `PR-body guards` red (run 41566264546, 02:27Z, "Another open PR already declares a fix for the same issue") fired while #29553 was still open; it closed at 02:30Z and the rerun 41566690516 on the same head is success, so the red is superseded. `Lint UI` is skipped by its path filter (no `ui/` path in the diff); the other nine queue-required contexts are success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` included.
6. **The `packages/lint` census pin 65 → 63 — right.** Two `==` literal comparisons left the `#7010 corpus` census for one `in`-list per form. #29639's `referenceNameVisible` row, merged in from `main`, is an `in`-list too, so the count holds on the merged head; `Test Core` is green.
7. **Regenerated artifacts — right.** `protocol.mdx` (1 row), `app-bundle.mdx` (5 rows, the same describe reached through the bundle's five item shapes) and `hook.mdx` (1 row) reproduce the describes verbatim; `check:generated` is green.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29415-user-delete-behavior-entry.md` carries `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two lines, line-initial. Right: what the diff publishes from a released package is describe / JSDoc text, a semantic entry and two form `visibleWhen` values, all in `@objectstack/spec`; `packages/lint` moves only a test; `content/docs/references` is generated output. Kind `none` takes `patch`. No `skip-changeset`, and none is wanted. `Clause-②: no` with no arm is right — nothing here widens or narrows an accept set; the narrowing is #29253's, and that pending note already declares `no (narrowing)`. `check-changeset-no-major` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6593885723: `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`, six `deviations`, each answered:

1. Attribution link points at the card thread — cosmetic, no action.
2. `protocol.zod.ts`: 1 of the 4 named sites edited — verified on the head. `GetMetaItemCachedResponseSchema.cascadeDeleteObjects` (≈2501) points at "the item read's `cascadeDeleteObjects`" and lists no kinds; the two `[#28001]` docblocks (≈646, ≈2480) say "the rule its delete walk runs" and list none. Nothing there implies a `user` field stays out. Right to leave.
3. The "Supersedes, in the same release" bullet with the #28001 note untouched — should-fix 1 in ④.
4. The hand-resolved merge in `field.form.ts` — verified on the head: #29639's `referenceNameVisible` row (an `in`-list) sits directly above the respelled `deleteBehavior` row; both are present and both gates serve.
5. No assignees or reviewers on `pr_create` — process, in line with the fleet-write rules.
6. Declaration lines before the 维护者速读 block — fine.

Inherited from #29553's report 6585093974, `out_of_scope_findings`: (a) `tree` has no `deleteBehavior` control — pre-existing, not moved by this PR; (b) the select has no empty option, so a stored value cannot be cleared from the form — verified in `SchemaForm.tsx`: both select branches render `value == null ? '' : String(value)` and offer no empty item; for `user` this is more than a convenience, should-fix 2 in ④; (c) the skills-docs follow-up #29400 is open.

Triage's should-fix on `59709cbb` ("AUTHORS one") is done at `field.zod.ts` ≈1834. Hold 6588339023's condition — the `cascadeDeleteObjects` describe after the freeze — is met; the freeze was lifted at 6588593530 on #28677. Nothing is escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

Each `hits` file, against the code it cites and its first consumer (the #29368 enforcement, read in `engine.ts` on this head):

- **`protocol.zod.ts`, `GetMetaItemResponseSchema.cascadeDeleteObjects`.** The describe now reads "a `master_detail` by default, a `lookup`, `tree` or `user` field that declares `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`". The engine agrees: `getCascadeDeleteObjects` walks `collectCascadeDeleteObjects` through `cascadeRelationBehavior`, whose family test `statesDeleteSemantics` admits a `user` field exactly when `deleteBehavior` is one of `DECLARED_DELETE_BEHAVIORS`; `deleteWalkTargetOf` answers `sys_user` for it whether or not a `reference` is spelled; the non-`master_detail` arm returns `fdef.deleteBehavior || 'set_null'`, and a `user` never reaches it undeclared, so a declared `cascade` resolves to `cascade`. So the `sys_user` object read names every object holding a `cascade` user field. Holds. Its consumer (`ui/packages/core/src/actions/recordDelete.ts`) reads the served list and keeps no copy of the rule.
- **`contracts/objectql-engine.ts`, `getCascadeDeleteObjects` docblock.** The same sentence; the re-wrap leaves one over-long line, cosmetic. Holds.
- **`data/field.zod.ts`.** ≈1831–1839: "reads it only on a `master_detail`, `lookup` or `tree` field that carries a `reference`, and on a `user` field that declares a `deleteBehavior`" is `statesDeleteSemantics` plus `deleteWalkTargetOf`, sentence for sentence. ≈2749 and the refusal message: "a `user` field has no default and keeps the id unless it declares one" — true, the `.overwrite` writes `set_null` on `lookup` / `tree` only and the engine invents no default ("⛔ No default is invented here"). ≈3316, the `.overwrite` comment — true. The runtime string carries no tracker number. Tried to break it: a `user` field with `deleteBehavior: 'set_null'` and `required: true`, single-valued — the engine escalates to `restrict` (`requiredSetNull && !multiValued`), a 409; `multiple: true` — deferred to the per-row judgement after the dependents probe, refused only where the remainder would be empty. That is exactly what the entry says. Holds.
- **`data/hook.zod.ts`.** `referentialFieldClear`: the `set_null` UPDATE resolves on `lookup` / `tree` by default and on a `user` field that declares it, never on `master_detail`. `referentialCascadeDelete`: `cascade` resolves on `master_detail` unless `restrict`, and on a declared `cascade` on `lookup`, `tree` or `user`. Both match `cascadeRelationBehavior`'s two arms. Holds.
- **`data/field.form.ts` and `data/object.form.ts`.** The predicates are disjoint and total over `lookup` / `user` / `master_detail`, and the pin is real: the test's evaluator parses `in`-lists with literal members and throws on any other spelling, `text` resolves to 0 controls, `user` to exactly 1 with all three values. The claim the design rests on — "the select does not prefill" — holds in the renderer: `SchemaForm.tsx`'s enum-fallback select seeds nothing from `schema.default` (`value == null ? ''`, the advertised `default: 'set_null'` is read nowhere on this path), so opening a `user` field in the designer and saving writes no `deleteBehavior`, and no unchosen `set_null` enters the walk. Tried to break it: once a value is chosen there is no empty item to return to "declares nothing", which for `user` is a distinct, enforced outcome (the id is kept, the field stays out of the walk) — only the Source tab clears it. See should-fix 2.
- **`migrations/entries/semantic/18.user-field-delete-behavior-enforced.ts`.** `surface` mirrors the precedent's spelling; `replacement` names the three outcomes and "drop the key"; `reason` states the old family (`DELETE_SEMANTICS_REFERENCE_TYPES`), the new rule, the pre-#9784 stored population and the `required` + `set_null` bound — every claim verified in `engine.ts` above; `acceptanceCriteria` is a consumer's own verify loop. The strings carry no tracker number. Holds.
- **`migrations/entries/semantic/18.user-field-foreign-reference-refused.ts`.** "which a `user` field that declares no `deleteBehavior` does not do" — true. Holds.

**Must-fix:** none.

**Should-fix:**

1. **The pending #28001 note is left false and corrected from elsewhere.** `.changeset/28001-cascade-delete-objects-beside-item.md` (unreleased on `main`) still says the cascading relations are "a `master_detail` by default, a `lookup` or `tree` that declares `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`", and it ships in the same release as #29253, so it is false on the day it is published. The "Supersedes, in the same release" bullet in the #29415 note is an erratum in a later entry — the shape the CHANGELOG guardrail names as the one a reader never reaches. The honest shape is the one this PR already takes for #29253's note: rewrite that one sentence in the pending #28001 note under the same DELIBERATE CORRECTION confirmation (same red, same class, this record's ①.3 extended by one sentence) and drop the Supersedes bullet. The published spec text is right either way, so the patch round is the lane's call.
2. **File a card for the form's missing empty option.** The Studio `deleteBehavior` select (both forms, through `SchemaForm.tsx`'s select widgets) offers no empty item, so on a `user` field a value once chosen cannot be returned to "declares nothing" from the form, and for `user` that absence is a distinct, enforced outcome. That is a metadata-authoring trap of the kind Prime Directive #10 says to file, not to note; the widget is `ui/`, so it is not this PR's to fix, but it should leave as an issue rather than an acceptance note.

**Landing condition:** the two `Check Changeset` reds are the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, confirmed by this record (each rewritten sentence judged in ①.3); the first `PR-body guards` red is superseded by the green rerun on the same head. No governed path is in the file list. The PR may enter the queue with the `Check Changeset` red named, under the landing-operations three conditions.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `abde58e1ebeeb1d9b90285689286c2f3ed755b0f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/objectql-engine.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.user-field-delete-behavior-enforced.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.user-field-foreign-reference-refused.ts + .changeset/28001-cascade-delete-objects-beside-item.md, .changeset/29415-user-delete-behavior-entry.md, .changeset/29253-user-field-delete-behavior.md, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs (the foreign-changeset rule), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts on the head (`cascadeRelationBehavior`, `statesDeleteSemantics`, `getCascadeDeleteObjects`), plus every cited file of record 6594347454

Delta record over record 6594347454 (PASS on `72a8bffd9fa53f37ade9a33e0e3e80ab0e825a27`), which adopted this seat's should-fix 1. `abde58e1` is exactly one commit on `72a8bffd` (parent verified with `git rev-list --parents`), no `main` merge, and its diff is +1 / −2 over two changeset files and nothing else (`git diff 72a8bffd abde58e1`): every `hits` file and every cited code file is byte-identical to the reviewed head. The ①, ②, ③ and ④ judgments of 6594347454 therefore carry unchanged, and this record judges only the delta.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set, exports, forms, entries: nothing moves.** The delta touches no file under `packages/`, `content/` or `ui/`; the 72a8bffd judgments on the accept set, the semantic entry, the forms and the regenerated artifacts stand as written.
2. **DELIBERATE CORRECTION of the unreleased #28001 note — right, judged sentence by sentence.** `.changeset/28001-cascade-delete-objects-beside-item.md` exists on the merge base, was not added by this PR, and is pending on `main`. The diff moves exactly one line of it (line 14, the **Served beside the object** bullet), and within that line exactly one parenthetical: "(a `master_detail` by default, a `lookup` or `tree` that declares `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`)" becomes "(a `master_detail` by default, a `lookup`, `tree` or `user` field that declares `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`)". The new sentence is true on the head and will be true on the day it ships: it is word for word the corrected `GetMetaItemResponseSchema.cascadeDeleteObjects` describe (judged in 6594347454 ④ against `cascadeRelationBehavior` → `statesDeleteSemantics`, which admits a `user` field exactly when it declares a `deleteBehavior`, so a declared `cascade` on a `user` field is named by `getCascadeDeleteObjects`). The old sentence would have been false in the same release as #29253. Every other sentence of the note — the frontmatter, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, the `Skills-docs:` line, the ETag, absence and `[]` statements, the objectql and spec bullets — is untouched, and nothing false is restored.
3. **The `Supersedes, in the same release` bullet is deleted from `.changeset/29415-user-delete-behavior-entry.md` — right.** It was the erratum-in-a-later-entry shape 6594347454 named; with the #28001 note itself corrected it had nothing left to say. The note's other bullets (Migration entry, Spec text, Studio forms), its frontmatter (`'@objectstack/spec': patch`) and both declaration lines are unchanged.
4. **The #29253 correction carries.** `.changeset/29253-user-field-delete-behavior.md` is byte-identical to `72a8bffd`; its two rewritten sentences were judged in 6594347454 ①.3 and that judgment stands.
5. **Gate verdicts on the head, as read at 2026-11-03T03:1xZ.** 46 runs: 13 success, 9 skipped, 1 failure, 23 in progress. The one failure is `Check Changeset` (job 125700476084), and its log is the #17712 foreign-changeset refusal on exactly two files — `.changeset/28001-cascade-delete-objects-beside-item.md` and `.changeset/29253-user-field-delete-behavior.md` — and nothing else; both are the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, both are judged here (item 2) and in 6594347454 (①.3), and this record is their confirmation under the landing rule 「其余(含改代码)照全套:同 head 达档复核 PASS 记录即确认,记录逐句判改写句」. A second `Check Changeset` run (job 125701086108) was still in progress; it reads the same two files and can only answer the same. `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` and `Spec property liveness` are success. The remaining in-progress runs — `Build Core`, `Test Core (1–8/8)`, the `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` lanes, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Live E2E UI` — read no changeset body, and the delta moves nothing else, so no verdict of theirs can turn on this delta; they were all success on `72a8bffd`. ⛔ This record does not claim them green: the seat adopting it reads them complete before it posts (see the landing condition).

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from 6594347454: `.changeset/29415-user-delete-behavior-entry.md` keeps `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the PR body carries the same two lines. The delta publishes nothing: it edits the text of two pending release notes and adds no changeset. The #28001 note's own frontmatter and declarations (`minor` on spec, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`) are untouched, so its level is not re-judged here.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The PR body's **Acceptance notes** now carry a paragraph naming the #28001 correction (patch round 1 at `abde58e1`, should-fix 1 of the contract review) and stating that `check-empty-changeset` reds on both files by design — read and found accurate against the tree and the job log.
- No new dev report on the card after 6593885723 at read time; no new `open_questions`. The 6594347454 ③ answers carry.
- Should-fix 2 of 6594347454 (file a card for the form's missing empty option) is not addressed by this delta and is not owed by it; it stays a should-fix, not a landing condition.
